proposal.title: Punch Trainer: Target Dummy Arena

mechanics.text: Core loop: Player character stands in a small arena facing a stationary Target Dummy. Pressing the punch input (default: left mouse click / gamepad X / keyboard F) triggers a punch animation on the player rig. On animation hit-frame, a hit-detection check (overlap/raycast from fist socket) determines if the dummy is within range. On successful hit: (1) play punch VFX (impact particle burst at contact point), (2) play punch SFX (whoosh + impact sound layered), (3) play dummy reaction (small knockback/flinch animation or physics impulse), (4) increment a persistent Hit Counter UI element by 1, (5) briefly flash/scale the counter text for feedback. Hit Counter persists for the session and resets on a 'Reset' button or key. Dummy has a fixed hitbox volume; no health/death state in this default scope (pure hit-tracking, not damage/KO). Punch has a short cooldown/animation-lock (~0.4s) to prevent spam-registering multiple hits per swing. Whiff (miss) attempts play swing SFX/VFX only, no counter increment. Optional combo window not included by default (single punch type only) to keep scope minimal.
assumptions: Single punch type (no combo strings, kicks, or special moves) unless expanded later.
Dummy is stationary and does not fight back, block, or die — it's a practice target, not an opponent.
Hit Counter is a simple incrementing integer shown as on-screen UI text, no persistence across sessions (resets on scene reload) unless a save system is requested.
One player-controlled character; no multiplayer/versus mode included.
Hit detection uses a simple overlap/trigger volume on the dummy rather than full physics-based collision resolution.
Camera is a fixed or simple follow camera focused on the player-dummy interaction; not specified so a basic third-person or side view is assumed.
VFX and SFX are single default punch impact assets (no combo-dependent variation) unless marketplace assets specify otherwise.
No damage numbers, health bars, or dummy destruction — scope is strictly a hit-counting trainer.
unresolved: Should the dummy ever reset position/respawn, or is it permanently fixed in place?
Is a Reset button/key for the Hit Counter desired, or should it count indefinitely with no reset option?
Should this be first-person, third-person, or 2D side-view for the punching perspective?

theme.text: A minimal, clean training-gym aesthetic centered on a single practice dummy and a player character in a combat stance, now bathed in a cool blue-lit atmosphere. The space reads as a modern dojo/gym bay lit primarily by blue-toned fixtures (e.g., cool blue overhead panels, rim lighting, or accent strips along the walls/floor), casting a focused blue glow on the dummy and player. Visual tone remains functional and readable over stylized — the priority is clear feedback (impact VFX, snappy animation, satisfying counter tick) rather than narrative or world-building. Think a late-night training bay vibe: neutral gray/dark surfaces contrasted by blue ambient and key lighting, with punchy, arcade-like impact effects (small spark/dust burst, brief screen feedback) that pop against the cool-toned backdrop to make each hit feel rewarding.
assumptions: No story, characters beyond the player and dummy, or narrative framing — this is a mechanics/skill-training sandbox.
Punch VFX styled as simple impact bursts (dust/spark particles) rather than exaggerated anime-style energy effects, unless otherwise specified.
SFX styled as realistic-ish punch/impact sounds (thud, whoosh) rather than cartoonish or sci-fi styled sounds.
Player character appearance/model is a placeholder/generic fighter rig unless specific character assets are requested.
Blue lighting is achieved via lighting/color-grading (cool blue key/ambient lights, blue accent fixtures) rather than changing overall environment geometry or layout.
Base surfaces (floor, walls) remain neutral gray/dark tones so the blue lighting reads clearly as the dominant color cue.

environment.text: Single small enclosed arena/room representing a training space (e.g., a gym floor or dojo mat). Layout: player spawns at a fixed position facing the Target Dummy, which is placed a short, fixed punching-range distance away. Hit Counter UI is docked in a fixed screen position (e.g., top-center or top-right) for constant visibility during practice. Minimal environment dressing — a floor, simple wall/backdrop, and basic ambient lighting — to keep focus on the player-dummy interaction. No additional NPCs, hazards, or secondary objects in this default scope.
assumptions: Static single-room environment; no level progression, multiple arenas, or exploration space.
Dummy position is fixed at scene start and does not move during gameplay (only reacts with hit animation/impulse).
Lighting is simple and functional (e.g., single directional/ambient setup) rather than dramatic or scene-specific.
Environment scale is small (single room, walking-distance interaction) rather than open-world.
